description: Byte-exact §6.4 signing preimages: preimage = uvarint(len(domain)) || domain || uvarint(len(messageType)) || messageType || uvarint(len(payloadFormat)) || payloadFormat || uvarint(len(schemaId)) || schemaId || uvarint(len(payload)) || payload, all strings UTF-8, uvarint = unsigned LEB128 of the BYTE length. 'schemaId' is a JSON string or null; null (absent schemaId) and the empty string are the same preimage, pinned by the schema-id-absent-null / schema-id-empty-string pair. 'payloadHex' is the exact payload bytes as lowercase hex (the suite's convention for byte inputs; payloads of 200/16383/16384 bytes and the 127/128-byte messageType are spelled out in full: byte i = i mod 256, respectively 't' repeated). The kind is accept-only: the preimage builder takes the domain as given, so there is no §6.4-mandated rejection to pin (malformed hex or a missing key is a malformed VECTOR, not a protocol rejection). The 'unit-golden-*' vectors port the five cases of persona-core-lib's SigningPreimageTest so both suites pin identical bytes.

vectors.description: Ported from the SigningPreimageTest unit golden 'single_small' (57 bytes): single-signed domain, absent schemaId (null), 3-byte payload — 1-byte length prefixes everywhere.

Ported from the unit golden 'multi_small' (63 bytes): identical fields under the multi-signed domain; the only difference from unit-golden-single-small is the domain, which pins domain separation (§6.4).
Ported from the unit golden 'single_schema' (107 bytes): present schemaId (40 lowercase hex) and the persona-binary payload format.
Ported from the unit golden 'single_200' (255 bytes): a 200-byte payload (byte i = i mod 256) whose length crosses the 1-byte uvarint boundary: uvarint(200) = c8 01.
Ported from the unit golden 'multi_empty' (110 bytes): empty payload under the multi-signed domain; uvarint(0) = 00.
Single-signed domain with empty messageType, payloadFormat and payload and an absent schemaId: the preimage is the domain followed by four 00 length prefixes. Hand-derived.
The same all-empty fields under the multi-signed domain.
Empty messageType and payloadFormat with a present schemaId and a 1-byte payload: only the schemaId contributes content bytes after the domain.
schemaId is JSON null (absent). §6.4 pins the absent case to the empty string, so this preimage must be byte-identical to schema-id-empty-string below.
schemaId is the empty string. Must be byte-identical to schema-id-absent-null: an absent and an empty schemaId are the same preimage (uvarint(0) = 00 and nothing else).
127-byte payload (byte i = i mod 256): the largest length that still fits one uvarint byte (7f).
128-byte payload (byte i = i mod 256): the first length that needs two uvarint bytes; uvarint(128) = 80 01. Hand-derived.
16383-byte payload (byte i = i mod 256): the largest length that fits two uvarint bytes; uvarint(16383) = ff 7f.
16384-byte payload (byte i = i mod 256): the first length that needs three uvarint bytes; uvarint(16384) = 80 80 01.
messageType of exactly 127 ASCII bytes ('t' x 127): the field length prefix is the single byte 7f.
messageType of exactly 128 ASCII bytes ('t' x 128): the field length prefix crosses to two bytes, 80 01.
messageType 'exämple.Grüß@v1' contains 2-byte UTF-8 characters (ä, ü, ß): the length prefix counts encoded bytes (18, prefix 12), not characters (15). Hand-derived.
payloadFormat 'jsön' is 5 UTF-8 bytes for 4 characters: the prefix is 05.

schemaId 'schema-🚀' ends in a 4-byte UTF-8 character: 11 bytes for 8 characters, prefix 0b. (A schemaId is normally 40 lowercase hex; the preimage treats it as an opaque UTF-8 string, which this vector pins.)

A non-standard domain: the preimage formula takes the domain as given (the two protocol domains are pinned by the vectors above); this pins that no implementation hard-codes the domain choice inside the formula.
